The legs are sewn as trousers in brushed flannel, continuing the same one-piece garment. The attached hood is sewn as a straw boater in sherpa. The suit is footless, so the footwear is left off. The sleeves end in plain finished cuffs. A fabric version of megaphone is stitched onto the suit. The garment is assembled from cut panels of fabric joined with visible seams, topstitching and piping, and it hangs as one coherent piece with every part in the outfit's own cloth. The uniform fills the whole straight-sided garment shape edge to edge, the same width at chest, waist and hem. It is a complete costume of carnival barker in one piece, shown full length from collar to ankles, with a striped waistcoat and a boater, trousers on the legs, a straw boater (as the hood), shoes (as the feet), a megaphone sewn or attached to the suit. The upper half carries the top and the leg tubes carry the lower garment, so the whole outfit reads at once. Novelty embellishments, rhinestone buttons down the front, soft chenille patches and fabric flames, stars or stripes sewn along the sleeves and legs. It is a novelty costume garment, made to be bright, playful, over-the-top and a pleasure to touch. Any printed skin is in a flat printed very deep brown skin tone.
